mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration persists but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 70% of such periods, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase below 50,000 persons while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0% indicates labor market softening, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units for three consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered episodes, or the median return is not below -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 3.5% and FEDFUNDS above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, increasing uncertainty and risk premiums, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% AND FEDFUNDS > 5.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 1.5% during a period when the unemployment rate is above 4.0% indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the median return is not below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.8% for four consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings and confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration persists but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.
